messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] error trying to run Distance 6.2
parts:
Derek

We receive reports of this regularly.  As you note, it has to do with privilege of using some of the file locations in Windows.  Even if you are not on a network, some versions of Windows are 'sensitive' to writing in certain directories.  Not clear which version of Windows you are using (7,8,10--note too there are 32 and 64 bit versions at least of 7).

a) Notice that Distance is trying to write to the location "C:\Users\Derek\AppData\Local\Temp\dstA96B.tmp".  Check to see if your administrator privilege will let you create such a file either in Windows Explorer or from the C> prompt.  That will verify whether the problem is a result of administrator privilege.

b) Note, that when I use Distance 6.2 on my Windows 7 machine, my log window shows a slightly different incarnation of the execution command:

C:\PROGRA~1\DISTAN~2\ec "C:\PROGRA~1\DISTAN~2\MCDS.exe 0, C:\DOCUME~1\eric\LOCALS~1\Temp\dst9F2.tmp \options 2>C:\DOCUME~1\eric\LOCALS~1\Temp\dst9F1.tmp"

Notice for me "Distance 6" has been transformed to "DISTAN~2" circumventing the offending space within the command string.  My version conforms to the DOS 8.3 file name convention (note the 10 character string "Distance 6" has been converted to an 8 character "DISTAN~2" string.

c) As a long-shot, print out your PATH (type "path" from the DOS prompt). 
  i) Does your current path contain "c:\windows\system32" ?
  ii) If no to i), see if adding "c:\windows\system32" to your path resolves the problem.

parts:
Sam

The very simplest way to avoid this problem is to install Distance to a location other than the default directory.  During the setup process of *all versions* of Distance, you are given the option of where to install Distance at this dialogue screen:

simply choose a directory that does not have spaces in the path.
